A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MaO research work. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and expanded evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and detector evaluations in the main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original benchmark evaluations, runtime measurements, a Stage A ablation, and detector-recall analyses.

M1.justification: The object-cropping pipeline, contrastive multi-object fine-tuning, and LeGrad-based descriptor optimization remain unchanged, including Equation (1). Applying MaO to SIGLIP and explaining single-vector backpropagation more explicitly do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds ILIAS, covering small, medium, and large objects, and PODS, whose average object area is approximately 20% of the image. This substantially extends evaluation beyond the retained small-object and clutter benchmarks. VoxDet-SoIR is a clarified name for the existing VoxDet retrieval benchmark.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds AMES across the original benchmarks while retaining the previous comparators. Appendix D adds Qwen2.5-VL as a pairwise-matching comparator, and Appendix C incorporates SIGLIP and linearly adapted backbone comparisons. These expand the comparison methods beyond simply extending existing baselines to another dataset.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce distractor-free ILIAS testing with mAP@1K, additional backbone configurations, a Qwen comparison using 100 queries and 200 gallery images with accuracy reporting, and separate encoding/search timing over 2,000 queries. The original training settings are retained. Newly explicit reranking descriptions do not establish that the retained Table 2 experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds a Stage A-only control, separating multi-object fine-tuning from subsequent optimization. Section 4.4 adds runtime analysis, and Tables F2–F3 examine detector recall by object size and clutter. The existing clutter experiment moves from Figure 3c to Figure F1; the regularization and iteration sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates; the existing descriptive dataset statistics are retained.

E6.justification: The original Table 2 scores remain unchanged, but many results are added. Examples include AMES at 48.68 mAP on VoxDet, Stage A at 75.04/63.14 on VoxDet/VoxDetW, and PODS MaO-CLIP/MaO-DINOv2 scores of 0.368/0.393. New ILIAS, Qwen, runtime, and detector-recall results further expand the evidence. These are additional results, not improved versions of the original scores.

T1.justification: The optimization objective and Appendix A's LeGrad formulation, Equations (1)–(5), are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical assumption is introduced; the explicit object-size ratio wording clarifies an existing measure.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain characterizing SoIR, introducing suitable benchmarks, and proposing a two-stage MaO framework producing a single descriptor. The abstract and contribution list retain the same principal superiority and scalability claims; additional experiments mainly supply supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning generalization to larger objects and another backbone, MLLM retrieval limitations, and the tradeoff between faster online search and more expensive offline encoding. Appendix F substantially expands detector-dependence discussion and newly identifies shortcomings on faces, individuals, and landmarks, while retaining the earlier occlusion and heavy-clutter limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link stating code/data availability, specifies comparator configurations and reranking participation, and reports additional encoding and OVD preprocessing costs. The optimizer, LoRA rank, batch size, hardware, and refinement settings remain unchanged. Actual availability of the linked resources cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: Related work gains a focused local-feature subsection and discussion of AMES and reranking transformers. New benchmark and modular-pipeline references include ILIAS, PODS, Grounded SAM, Open3DIS, and TROY-VIS. These extend the existing positioning around compact retrieval and detector-based representations without replacing its central novelty argument.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with localized rewrites and clearer explanations of object proposals and unified-vector optimization. VoxDet gains the VoxDet-SoIR name, a runtime subsection is inserted, and the appendix reorganizes detector evaluation and limitations. This is a limited narrative revision rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figure 1 is redesigned, Figure 3's clutter panel becomes Appendix Figure F1, and the resolution axis changes from resize scale to image size. New tables, expanded ablation/comparison tables, revised captions, and corrected plot legends substantially alter presentation.

improvement.justification: The Stage A-only control resolves an important attribution gap, while detector breakdowns substantially strengthen failure analysis beyond v1's aggregate recall. AMES and the additional datasets broaden validation, and runtime reporting exposes the practical online/offline cost tradeoff. These materially strengthen the empirical case. Some additions remain weaker: ILIAS excludes distractors, the Qwen protocol is sparsely specified, and Appendix C overstates DINOv2-based superiority relative to Table C1, where adapted SIGLIP scores 58.70 against MaO-DINOv2's 48.85.
